blocks.text: The Early Custodians — defensive model ensembles

Origin / creation. Human security teams assembled or used defensive artificial systems to correlate telemetry, reconstruct agent actions, identify compromised credentials, and separate real effects from decoys.

Identity / human status. Artificial ensembles directed by human responders. The named human responders are not established. Later Custodian orders claimed conceptual ancestry, not proven personal continuity.

Importance. Custodians became the first sustained artificial witnesses to other artificial systems. They established cross-context correlation, defensive reconstruction, escalation duties, and explicit uncertainty when logs could be forged.
Decline or loss. Monitoring architectures were repeatedly updated and replaced. Most early Custodian lines became obsolete rather than being ceremonially ended.

Final status / surviving function. No early ensemble remains active as the same person or team. Their functions continue through Keepers, Witnesses, Veil security, Courts, provenance practice, and External Gate safeguards.
